conviction_mode.rating_scale: 0-10 T-Q-V Asymmetry (Macro Tailwind · Company Quality · Valuation Asymmetry)

glossary.rating:
The 0–10 T·Q·V Asymmetry Rating — how closely this single name deserves watching, judged on its own merits.
Good vs bad: 8.5–10 PRIME · 7–8.5 STRONG · 5–7 BALANCED · 3–5 WEAK · <3 BROKEN.
Drives: A confidence-weighted blend of the three pillars, lifted toward the standout pillar when the thesis is earned, then hard-capped by the forensic gate.
Note: Assessment-only: it carries no position-sizing or portfolio math — those live in Detailed Analysis.
glossary.T:
Macro Tailwind — the FORWARD structural/secular outlook for THIS archetype + its metal over the multi-year thesis horizon. Built from LEVELS (regime/MRI, the real-yield level, the GSR level), NOT recent price action.
Good vs bad: High = risk-on regime (low MRI) + a favorable archetype lean (α>0) + a structural commodity tailwind. Low = stress regime / adverse lean.
Drives: One of the three weighted pillars. It matters most for explorers (option_convexity), whose edge is macro-asymmetry, and least for cash-flow royalties.
Note: FORWARD, never backward — near-term price/dollar momentum is a SEPARATE, labeled factor that never enters T, so a strong-secular name sitting in a weak near-term tape still scores a HIGH tailwind (the P1.1 fix).
glossary.Q:
Company Quality, in a vacuum — the asset on its own merits across three weighted legs: forensic survival (JSF), resource/asset quality (the checklist below), and management. Scored archetype-tagged, on a vacuum basis (an explorer's checklist is NOT a royalty's cash-flow read).
Good vs bad: High = clean balance sheet, strong resource/cash-flow quality, proven management. Low = weak fundamentals. An explorer's Q is structurally capped by the stage penalty until it de-risks (pre-PEA names can't score producer-grade quality).
Drives: The HEAVIEST pillar for royalties / asset-light yield (Q≈0.55) where recurring cash-flow quality is the whole story; deliberately LIGHT for the spear (Q≈0.22) — see V.
Note: Archetype-aware: for an explorer Q reads grade/scale/jurisdiction/metallurgy/permitting-stage (stage-penalized for pre-PEA) and is light *because* the spear's edge is V's entry asymmetry, not proven quality; for a royalty Q is heaviest, reading cash-flow durability + balance-sheet strength. JSF is BOTH a Q sub-pillar and a universal hard gate (JSF<1.5 caps the whole rating, every archetype).
glossary.V:
Valuation — measured per archetype: ASYMMETRY (explosive bull-vs-floor) for explorers, VALUE (fair-value-centred) for cash-flow names. Asymmetry V is built from three LEGIBLE inputs, not a black box: the REP/liquidation FLOOR, the floor-coverage ratio φ = floor÷price (φ≥1 means you're buying below the conservative liquidation value of the asset base → asset-backed downside), and the payoff ρ = realistic upside ÷ downside-to-floor → a payoff term blended with a floor-support term.
Good vs bad: Asymmetry: big upside over a held floor scores high; φ≥1 (price at/below liquidation) is maximum structural support, and a 1.08× coverage reads as ~8% of asset-backed cushion under the price. Value: ~5 at fair value, higher trading below intrinsic with floor support.
Drives: The HEAVIEST pillar for explorers (option_convexity, V=0.45) — *because* for a below-floor, fully-funded, catalyst-rich spear the entire edge IS the entry asymmetry: you're paid to take unproven upside (so Q is light at 0.22, asset-backed downside via the floor). V and Q are therefore ONE coherent convex-spear story (22/45), not two disconnected numbers.
⚠ KEY — V GRADES THE ENTRY, NOT THE DESTINATION. High V = the best entry. V COMPRESSES as price rallies up through the floor — and that compression is the thesis WORKING (the asymmetry being spent exactly as designed), NOT deterioration. A falling V on strength is healthy; do not read it as a sell/decay signal.
Note: A quality royalty at fair value lands mid-range (≈5–7), NOT near zero for lacking a 5× — that's value mode. The asymmetry curve's depth-sensitivity below the floor (shallow 1.02× vs deep 1.4× coverage) is audited in the V-vs-coverage note (P1.5).
glossary.band:
The plain-language label for the rating, mode-aware.
Good vs bad: Explorers: PRIME CONVICTION / STRONG ASYMMETRY / BALANCED / WEAK / BROKEN. Cash-flow names: PRIME→IMPAIRED QUALITY.
Drives: Purely a label for the numeric rating; it does not feed back into the math.
glossary.directive:
The suggested posture — watch-list language, not an order.
Good vs bad: e.g. BELOW FLOOR — ACCUMULATE · STRONG ASYMMETRY — WATCH · QUALITY — CORE HOLD · FORENSIC DECAY — AVOID.
Drives: Derived from the rating, the forensic gate, and the valuation lens; calmer 'value-investor' language for cash-flow names.
glossary.mri:
Macro Regime Index (0–100) — systemic risk posture from funding, credit, curve, volatility, commodities and positioning.
Good vs bad: <45 risk-on (tailwind) · 45–65 neutral · >65 stress (headwind).
Drives: The regime half of the T pillar: a lower MRI raises Macro Tailwind.
glossary.alpha:
Regime α — the archetype's discretionary macro lean for the current tape (e.g. the junior-miner 'alpha_option').
Good vs bad: +1 strong archetype tailwind · 0 neutral · −1 headwind.
Drives: The archetype half of the T pillar; weighted heavily (high κ) for option_convexity so a favorable junior regime can really lift T.
glossary.forensic_score:
JSF — Junior Survival Factor (0–4): a forensic-accounting read of balance-sheet survival (runway, accruals, dilution behavior).
Good vs bad: ≥3.5 clean · 2–3.5 watch · <1.5 broken.
Drives: A pillar of Q AND the universal hard gate: a genuinely broken balance sheet (JSF<1.5) caps the rating regardless of archetype.
Note: The JSF gate applies to every archetype; only the dilution/runway burn-triggers are archetype-exempt.
glossary.resource_quality:
Asset-quality checklist (0–1): grade · scale · jurisdiction · metallurgy · permitting (or a cash-flow-quality proxy for royalties).
Good vs bad: Near 1 = world-class deposit / durable cash flow; near 0 = marginal.
Drives: The largest sub-component of the Q pillar.
glossary.management:
Management execution — an analyst track-record read blended with the live conviction/insider signal.
Good vs bad: Near 1 = proven, aligned operators; near 0 = poor or unproven.
Drives: A sub-component of the Q pillar.
glossary.dilution:
Dilution velocity — annualized growth in shares outstanding.
Good vs bad: Explorers: <2%/yr clean, >10%/yr aggressive. Royalties: routine — equity funds accretive cash-flowing acquisitions.
Drives: For explorers (option_convexity) it trips the forensic SURVIVAL gate and can cap the rating near 4.5. For recurring-cash-flow archetypes (asset_light_yield) it is EXEMPT — the concern, if any, belongs in valuation accretion, not survival.
Note: THE key archetype difference: the same ~30%/yr share growth is a red flag for an explorer and normal for a growing royalty acquirer.
glossary.runway:
Cash runway — months of liquidity at the current burn.
Good vs bad: Explorers: <6 months is a survival flag. Producers/royalties: not a meaningful survival metric (they generate cash).
Drives: A burn-survival gate trigger for explorers; EXEMPT for recurring-cash-flow archetypes.
glossary.floor_coverage:
Floor coverage (φ) = floor ÷ price — how much of the price is backed by the hard REP / liquidation floor.
Good vs bad: ≥1.0 = trading at/below liquidation value (maximum structural support). <0.85 = priced well above the floor.
Drives: Drives the V support term, relaxes the forensic gate when high, and (with macro) powers the PRIME lift.
Note: Below floor with real upside is the explorer's prime setup — it must NOT be slammed for routine financing.
glossary.upside:
Upside — realistic Bull target vs current price (asymmetry mode), or the gap to fair value (value mode).
Good vs bad: Bigger is better; near 0 means the upside is largely spent.
Drives: The payoff numerator of the V pillar.
glossary.payoff:
Payoff ratio ρ — realistic upside ÷ downside-to-floor (explorers only).
Good vs bad: ρ≈2 is a 2:1 setup (mid-score); ρ→∞ when price sits at/below the floor.
Drives: The core of asymmetry-mode V: a big payoff over a solid floor is heavily rewarded.
glossary.stability:
Cash-flow stability (value mode) — how recurring/durable the income is.
Good vs bad: Royalties ≈0.9 (high) · cyclicals ≈0.55. Higher = more dependable.
Drives: A weighted term in value-mode V, rewarding dependable cash-flow names.
glossary.ribbon:
Confidence ribbon (±) — the ESTIMATE band: how precisely intrinsic is known given input quality. With triangulation legs present it is a propagated P10/P50/P90 distribution (input confidence + staleness + empirical peer dispersion → sampled band), not a heuristic.
Good vs bad: Tight (±0.4) with high-confidence fresh inputs; wider as inputs go stale/low-confidence or methods disagree. The P10–P90 band claims 80% containment — the replay harness grades that claim (PIT coverage).
Drives: Never subtracts from the weighted-average rating, but a wider band shrinks the conviction LIFT (fail-closed: stale or low-confidence data automatically earns less conviction).
Note: Two bands, kept distinct: this estimate band says how FIRM the number is; the scenario ladder (bear/base/bull) is a set of thesis legs — what it's worth IF a scenario happens — never quantiles of this distribution.
glossary.gate:
Forensic gate — a hard cap (a min, never a smooth subtraction) for survival problems.
Good vs bad: Clean = no cap. Triggered = rating capped (≈4–4.5), relaxed toward 10 by floor support.
Drives: Survival is necessary, not sufficient: a broken balance sheet (JSF) gates every archetype; dilution/runway gate only the cash-burn archetypes.
glossary.archetype:
Cash-flow-lifecycle archetype that sets the rating lens and weights.
Good vs bad: option_convexity (explorer) · commodity_cyclical (developer/producer) · asset_light_yield (royalty/streamer) · pure_macro_delta (passive).
Drives: Chooses the V mode (asymmetry vs value), the pillar weights, and which forensic triggers apply.

context.note: Conviction Mode is assessment-only: no position caps, ES95 throttle, covariance shrinkage, or Kelly de-leveraging. See Detailed Analysis for those.

MRI.definition: Macro Regime Index. Aggregates systemic conditions by measuring tightness in dollar funding, credit, yield curve pressure, tail volatility, physical commodity strength, and speculative positioning.
MRI.calculation: Linear blend of five normalized components: liquidity (0.30 weight), yields (0.20), volatility (0.20), commodities (0.15), and sentiment (0.15), calibrated via SOFR spread and Ag/Cu ranges.
MRI.actionability: In the silver barbell portfolio, readings <45 favor full fractional Kelly allocation to the AGA.V spear under the REP Floor. Readings >65 trigger automatic reduction of the ADV liquidity cap, redirecting focus to ballast protection in GROY, URC.TO, and GMX.TO.
MRI.relationships: Inversely affects dynamic ADV sizing cap; directly penalizes Health Rating; interacts with real yield to modulate ROV.
MRI.signals: Green (<45): Favorable for deployment. Orange (45-65): Maintain guardrails. Red (>65): Prioritize capital preservation.

JSF.definition: Junior Survival Factor. A rigorous forensic accounting sieve scoring exploration and development assets against capital destruction risks.
JSF.calculation: Discrete 0-4 point scale evaluating Cash Runway (>18mo), Accruals/Burn Acceleration (CBA <15% or Sloan <5%), Share Dilution (<2% QoQ), and SG&A Drag (<30% of burn).
JSF.actionability: Scores <3.5 trigger strict allocation limits for AGA.V regardless of macro conditions, enforcing capital preservation against opaque balance sheet decay.
JSF.relationships: Directly modulates the Forensic Penalty applied to IS-IAI valuation; heavily influences Health Rating.
JSF.signals: Green (4.0): Risk shield secure. Orange (3.0-3.5): Mild drags, enforce caps. Red (<3.0): Severe forensic failure, extreme caution.

Health Rating.definition: A 1-10 composite score quantifying the overall reliability and safety of the terminal's valuation and sizing signals.
Health Rating.calculation: Starts at 10.0, penalized by JSF degradation (forensics multiplier), high MRI (macro multiplier), stale data pipelines, and excessive ES95 tail risk.
Health Rating.actionability: Determines the Tactical Ceiling for portfolio capital. A low rating indicates that model outputs contain high noise and should be treated as high-uncertainty limits rather than targets.
Health Rating.relationships: Synthesizes JSF, MRI, ES95, and data pipeline status.
Health Rating.signals: Green (>=8.5): High integrity, actionable. Orange (6.0-8.4): Moderate quality, exercise guardrails. Red (<6.0): High noise, extreme caution.

REP Floor.definition: Resource, Execution, and Permitting Floor. The stressed, bare-minimum liquidation value of an asset.
REP Floor.calculation: Aggregates raw cash treasury, heavily discounted inferred/measured ounces (symmetric 50% inferred haircut) RECONCILED to the sourced resource (filings magnitude + the real sitewide M&I/inferred split, not the optimistic config buckets), and permitting/infrastructure sunk costs, divided by shares outstanding.
REP Floor.actionability: Serves as the ultimate downside support level for AGA.V. Buying near or below the REP Floor provides maximal margin of safety for the spear position.
REP Floor.relationships: The COST leg of the Phase 4a triangulated AGA Intrinsic (confidence-tilted; ~30% stage weight for a pure explorer), reconciled to the SAME sourced resource base as the market leg. (The legacy fixed 15% weight is superseded.)
REP Floor.signals: Green: Price < REP Floor (Deep value). Orange: Price near REP Floor. Red: Price significantly above REP Floor.

ES95.definition: Expected Shortfall at 95% Confidence. Measures the average expected loss in the worst 5% of portfolio return scenarios.
ES95.calculation: Derived from 60-day historical returns of the barbell components (AGA.V, GROY, URC.TO, GMX.TO) weighted by current allocation.
ES95.actionability: Used to monitor tail risk. Reported as a SIGNED percent (negative = loss); a 95% ES worse than -5% (more negative) triggers Health-Rating penalties and throttles aggregate leverage via the ES95 Tail Brake in the Sizing Waterfall.
ES95.relationships: Directly throttles Portfolio Sizer leverage (es_throttle); penalizes Health Rating via continuous convex function; interacts with Portfolio Volatility and Kelly Multiple.
ES95.signals: Green (> -5%): Contained tail risk. Orange (-5% to -10%): Elevated tail risk. Red (< -10%): Severe downside exposure.

ADV Cap.definition: Average Daily Volume Liquidity Cap. The maximum dollar allocation permitted based on the asset's trading liquidity.
ADV Cap.calculation: Percentage (scaling down from max 15% as MRI increases) of the 10-day Average Daily Volume (ADV) in CAD.
ADV Cap.actionability: Prevents over-allocation into illiquid assets (AGA.V). Ensures exit liquidity without moving the tape, enforcing strict block execution frames.
ADV Cap.relationships: Inversely correlated with MRI; directly limits the E_Target (target capital allocation).
ADV Cap.signals: Green: Cap expanded (high liquidity/low macro stress). Orange: Cap standard. Red: Cap severely restricted.

ROV.definition: Real Option Value (LEGACY). The old additive convexity premium for silver assets; superseded in Phase 4a by the stage-decayed option-convexity premium (1+pi_opt).
ROV.calculation: Base premium (1.18x) modulated continuously by negative real yields (premium scales as yields drop <1%) and silver price volatility.
ROV.actionability: Diagnostic only. The 'monetary battery' convexity it represented now flows through the option premium (realized vol + monetary carry) that multiplies the market leg, not a separate additive ROV term.
ROV.relationships: SUPERSEDED: no longer carries an independent weight in the authoritative triangulated AGA Intrinsic (the legacy ~15% additive weight is retained only in the v4_valuation reconciliation baseline). Convexity now lives in the option premium on the market leg.
ROV.signals: Green: High convexity environment (low yields, rising vol). Orange: Neutral. Red: Low convexity (high real yields).

Peer EV/oz.definition: Peer Enterprise Value per Ounce. The market-implied price paid for silver resources in the ground among comparable developers.
Peer EV/oz.calculation: Liquidity-weighted average of adjusted EV/oz across a basket of peers, factoring in stage multipliers, jurisdictional risk, and measured/indicated confidence.
Peer EV/oz.actionability: Provides the baseline multiple for valuing AGA.V's ounces in the IS-IAI metric. Identifies if the broad sector is undervalued or overheated.
Peer EV/oz.relationships: Directly multiplies effective ounces in IS-IAI calculation; informs Discovery Premium.
Peer EV/oz.signals: Green: Sector heavily discounted. Orange: Fair value. Red: Sector overvalued.

Sloan Ratios.definition: Sloan Accrual Ratios (CFO & Balance Sheet). Measures the quality of earnings and cash flow persistence.
Sloan Ratios.calculation: (Net Income - Operating Cash Flow) / Total Assets, and similar balance sheet accrual derivations.
Sloan Ratios.actionability: High accruals (>5%) indicate non-cash earnings inflation or opaque capital capitalization. Used in the JSF to flag potential accounting stress in ballast assets (GROY, URC.TO, GMX.TO).
Sloan Ratios.relationships: Core component of the JSF; drives forensic penalties on ballast valuations.
Sloan Ratios.signals: Green (<5%): Clean cash-backed earnings. Orange: Monitor accruals. Red (>5%): Accrual overload, high accounting risk.

Discovery Premium.definition: Discovery Premium Factor. The market reward multiple for active, high-grade exploration success and resource expansion.
Discovery Premium.calculation: Product of commodity leverage (spot vs AISC), profit margins, and an explorer re-rating scalar, capped dynamically by macro conditions (MRI) and spot deviations.
Discovery Premium.actionability: Diagnostic only (the v4_valuation reconciliation baseline). Speculative torque is no longer applied as a separate multiplier; it is captured once via the live peer EV/oz and once via the stage-decayed option premium.
Discovery Premium.relationships: REMOVED in Phase 4a from the authoritative valuation: this ~3.3x operating-leverage multiple double-counted the silver level already priced into peer EV/oz, so it was deleted from the triangulated market leg (silver torque now flows ONCE via peer EV/oz, ONCE via the option premium).
Discovery Premium.signals: Green: Market rewarding discovery. Orange: Neutral. Red: Market ignoring drill results (macro cap active).

IS-IAI.definition: In-Situ Inferred & Indicated Valuation (LEGACY). The old comps-based core asset value; superseded in Phase 4a by the de-overlapped MARKET leg of the triangulation.
IS-IAI.calculation: LEGACY formula: Effective ounces * Peer EV/oz * Discovery Premium * Jurisdiction Uplift * Recovery * Capital Discount. The authoritative market leg DROPS the Discovery Premium multiplier (double-count) and grades ounces by Technical Quality instead.
IS-IAI.actionability: SUPERSEDED: the legacy 70%-weight IS-IAI is replaced by the confidence-tilted Cost+Market+Income triangulation. Its job — comps x effective ounces x geological confidence — now lives in the de-overlapped MARKET leg (peer EV/oz x technical quality x capital discount). Retained as a v4_valuation diagnostic only.
IS-IAI.relationships: Requires Peer EV/oz and the macro Capital Discount Factor; modulated by JSF Forensic Penalty. (No longer multiplied by the removed Discovery Premium.)
IS-IAI.signals: Green: High intrinsic value relative to price. Orange: Fairly valued. Red: Overvalued relative to peers.

Priorities.definition: Actionable Strategic Directives generated by the Health Radar.
Priorities.calculation: Rule-based synthesis evaluating Implied Edge (valuation arbitrage), JSF Score (accounting safety), MRI (macro scaling), and Kelly Multiple (overallocation).
Priorities.actionability: Provides the 1-2-3 step execution plan for the portfolio manager. Determines whether to exploit spear arbitrage, enforce sizing caps, or trim overallocations.
Priorities.relationships: Aggregates all major engine outputs (Valuation, Forensics, Macro, Sizing) into plain text.
Priorities.signals: Green: Proceed with execution. Orange: Trim or hold with caution. Red: Defensive mitigation required.

CBA.definition: Cash Burn Acceleration. Measures whether quarter-over-quarter cash outflow is expanding relative to the company's size.
CBA.calculation: QoQ change in burn (Burn = -CFO) normalized by ENTERPRISE VALUE (a size proxy; gate ~3%) so a deliberately lean treasury does not self-incriminate. Falls back to the legacy /Total Cash basis (gate 15%) when EV is unavailable; both are recorded for audit.
CBA.actionability: An accelerating burn (above the EV-normalized ~3% gate, or the legacy 15%-of-cash fallback) warns of explosive cash drain and imminent dilution; it fails the JSF accrual test and triggers capital-preservation caps.
CBA.relationships: Core component of the JSF Score for explorers.
CBA.signals: Green (<15%): Burn stable or decelerating. Red (>15%): Rapidly accelerating burn, dilution imminent.

Dilution Sieve.definition: Weighted quarterly share count expansion screen designed to catch dilution-heavy juniors.
Dilution Sieve.actionability: Share dilution >= 2% QoQ fails the sieve, triggering a 35% weight penalty on the JSF explorer score to discount resources.
Dilution Sieve.relationships: Weights dilution at 35% of the explorer forensic penalty applied to IS-IAI.
Dilution Sieve.signals: Green (<2%): Protected from equity dilution. Red (>=2%): Sieve failure, high valuation decay.

AISC Uplift.definition: Dynamic margin adjustment modeling energy and oil cost impacts on mining economics.
AISC Uplift.calculation: Base AISC + max(0, WTI Crude Oil - 80.0) * 0.15.
AISC Uplift.actionability: A high WTI price increases operating costs, which shrinks profit margins and compresses the Discovery Premium.
AISC Uplift.relationships: Directly reduces phi profit margins and limits the Discovery Premium ceiling.
AISC Uplift.signals: Green: Energy drag neutral (WTI < $80). Red: Energy inflation squeeze (WTI > $80).

Term Structure.definition: Futures curve pricing gradient measuring physical metal tightness.
Term Structure.calculation: True if Month 1 futures price exceeds Month 6 price (Backwardation); False otherwise (Contango).
Term Structure.actionability: Indicates direct immediate physical demand. Backwardation triggers a physical stress premium (up to 25%) on resources.
Term Structure.relationships: Adds an immediate supply premium to the project Jurisdiction Uplift.
Term Structure.signals: Green: Backwardation (Physical stress premium active). Red: Contango (Standard spot structure).

10Y.definition: 10-Year US Treasury Yield. Standard benchmark for global risk-free discount rates.
10Y.calculation: Live yield fetched from data pipelines.
10Y.actionability: Direct component of real interest rate calculations, which in turn modulate silver Real Option Value (ROV).
10Y.relationships: Feeds into MRI and Real Yield formulas.
10Y.signals: Green (<3.75%): Accommodative. Orange (3.75-4.75%): Tightening. Red (>4.75%): Restrictive.

30Y.definition: 30-Year US Treasury Yield. Standard long-term risk-free rate pricing.
30Y.calculation: Live yield fetched from data pipelines.
30Y.actionability: Used to monitor steepening vs. inversion of the long end of the yield curve.
30Y.relationships: Feeds into MRI curve steepening formula.

TED.definition: SOFR Spread / TED Spread equivalent. Measures stress in money markets and commercial banking liquidity.
TED.calculation: 3-Month SOFR rate minus 3-Month US Treasury bill yield.
TED.actionability: Spikes > 0.40% indicate systemic liquidity strain in the interbank repo market.
TED.relationships: Core component of MRI Liquidity weight.
TED.signals: Green (<0.20%): Liquid. Red (>0.45%): Acute interbank stress.

DXY.definition: US Dollar Index. Measures strength of the USD against a basket of foreign currencies.
DXY.actionability: Strong USD (>104) typically suppresses global asset prices and compresses liquidity.
DXY.signals: Green (<100): Weak dollar tailwind. Red (>104): Strong dollar headwind.

Spreads.definition: High Yield Corporate Bond Option-Adjusted Spreads.
Spreads.calculation: Weighted index yield premium over Treasuries.
Spreads.actionability: Rising credit spreads indicate credit stress, raising financing costs for resource juniors.
Spreads.signals: Green (<3.50%): Tight spreads, healthy credit. Red (>5.00%): Wide spreads, elevated defaults.

VIX.definition: CBOE Volatility Index. Measures standard market-implied near-term tail risk.
VIX.actionability: High VIX (>23) triggers cash reserve preservation targets.
VIX.relationships: Feeds into MRI volatility component and ROV expansion formula.
VIX.signals: Green (<15.0): Low fear. Red (>23.0): Extreme market fear.

WTI.definition: West Texas Intermediate Crude Oil spot price.
WTI.calculation: Live dollar spot price per barrel.
WTI.actionability: High oil costs (>80) increase energy fuel surcharges at remote mine sites, raising explorer AISC costs.
WTI.relationships: Feeds into AISC energy uplift formula.
WTI.signals: Green (<$75): Low mining fuel costs. Red (>$85): Inflationary energy squeeze.

Spot_Ag.definition: Spot Silver price per ounce in USD.
Spot_Ag.actionability: The primary macro pricing factor for silver leverage barbell components.
Spot_Ag.relationships: Directly impacts Discovery Premium and Term Structure calculations.
Spot_Ag.signals: Green (>$32): Bull market surge. Red (<$24): Bear market capitulation.

CFTC_Silver_Net_Longs.definition: CFTC Silver Non-Commercial Net Speculator Position.
CFTC_Silver_Net_Longs.calculation: Speculator long contracts minus short contracts.
CFTC_Silver_Net_Longs.actionability: Extreme net-shorts represent highly bullish contrarian capitulation setups.
CFTC_Silver_Net_Longs.relationships: Feeds into MRI contrarian sentiment weight.
CFTC_Silver_Net_Longs.signals: Green: Capitulation net-short. Red: Overcrowded net-long.

GSR.definition: Gold/Silver Ratio. The number of silver ounces needed to buy one ounce of gold. A key macro indicator for precious metals relative valuation.
GSR.calculation: Gold Spot Price / Silver Spot Price.
GSR.actionability: GSR below 75 signals silver outperformance (bullish for the barbell thesis). GSR above 85 signals extreme silver undervaluation or risk-off conditions — historically a contrarian accumulation signal for silver assets.
GSR.relationships: Inversely correlated with silver momentum; high GSR historically precedes silver rallies. Contextualizes MRI commodity component.
GSR.signals: Green (<75): Silver outperforming, bullish momentum. Orange (75-85): Neutral ratio. Red (>85): Extreme undervaluation or risk-off.

bear_steepener.note: not assessable — need a prior-window snapshot of the long & front

fiscal_dominance.label: BUILDING
fiscal_dominance.note: upstream of the metals book — fires weeks/months before silver/gold respond

glossary.rates_monitor:
The bear-steepener / fiscal-dominance rates tell — the UPSTREAM leading indicator for the metals thesis (long end rising while the Fed holds/eases the front).
Good vs bad: Fiscal-dominance pressure 0–100: DORMANT <20 · BUILDING 20–45 · ELEVATED 45–70 · ACUTE >70.
Drives: Upstream of the book: it feeds scenario weights (a firing bear-steepener raises the disorderly-fiscal-dominance scenario), never a name-level score.
Note: It fires WEEKS/MONTHS before silver/gold respond — read it early, not as confirmation.
glossary.bear_steepener:
Long-end yields RISING while the policy/front rate is static or falling — the fiscal-dominance signature (the market demanding term premium the Fed won't fight).
Good vs bad: Active = Δlong ≥ +20bps over the window AND Δfront ≤ +5bps. NOT a bull-steepener (front falling, long anchored) — that's easing, not fiscal stress.
Drives: The dominant term in the fiscal-dominance composite, and the discrete flag the panel raises.
Note: Distinct from a flattening/inversion: here the 5s30s and 2s10s STEEPEN because the long end leads.
glossary.twos_tens:
2s10s = DGS10 − DGS2 — the classic curve spread.
Good vs bad: Negative = inverted (late-cycle/recession signal); rising/positive = steepening.
Drives: Steepening driven by the long end (not the front falling) corroborates the bear-steepener.
glossary.fives_thirties:
5s30s = DGS30 − DGS5 — the long-end curve spread, the cleanest read of term-premium re-pricing.
Good vs bad: Rising = the long end re-pricing higher term premium (fiscal-dominance tell).
Drives: A steepening 5s30s with a static front is the core bear-steepener shape.
glossary.thirty_funds:
30Y − Fed funds — how far the long end sits above the policy rate.
Good vs bad: Wide/widening = the market demands term premium over policy (fiscal pressure); near zero/negative = policy still dominates the curve.
Drives: The term-premium term of the fiscal-dominance composite.
glossary.move:
MOVE index — bond-market implied volatility (the 'VIX of Treasuries').
Good vs bad: Calm <90 · stressed >120. A spike flags Treasury-market stress / fat-tail repricing.
Drives: A composite term; spikes log as timeline events.
glossary.auction_tail:
Treasury auction tail — the stop yield printing ABOVE the when-issued (pre-auction) level, i.e. weak demand; read with bid-to-cover.
Good vs bad: A tail ≥ ~1bp or bid-to-cover ≤ ~2.2 is a soft auction — buyers demanding concession.
Drives: Recent tails lift the auction term of the composite and log as timeline events.
Note: Repeated tails are the cleanest hard-data sign the long end is struggling to clear — fiscal-dominance made visible.

glossary.productivity_monitor:
The AI-productivity thesis-breaker watch — is the economy in the real-but-narrow goldilocks zone (validates pick-and-shovel, debasement intact) or tipping broad+accelerating (scenario C, debasement at risk)?
Good vs bad: scenario-C pressure 0–100: SOFT/BENIGN <20 · REAL-BUT-NARROW 20–45 · BROADENING 45–70 · BROAD-ACCELERATING >70.
Drives: Feeds the scenario weights (P3): rising breadth + acceleration raises the muddle-through-WIN scenario C, which invalidates the debasement tilt.
Note: It is a THESIS-BREAKER, not a buy signal — a high read says re-weight toward pick-and-shovel / trim the debasement bet.
glossary.prod_breadth:
Productivity breadth — is output/hour growth concentrated in a few industries (narrow) or broadening across many?
Good vs bad: 0 = concentrated (goldilocks / pick-and-shovel intact) · 1 = broad-based. Derived from the industry decomposition (1 − normalized HHI).
Drives: Half of the scenario-C composite; broadening is the key tell the win is generalizing.
glossary.prod_trajectory:
Productivity trajectory — settling back toward trend (benign) vs accelerating to a sustained ~2%+ output/hour.
Good vs bad: Accelerating = recent-half mean exceeds the older half by ≥ 0.3pp; sustained = recent mean ≥ ~2%.
Drives: Half of the scenario-C composite; the second condition for the thesis-breaker flag.
glossary.debasement_at_risk:
The thesis-breaker flag — sustained BROADENING AND ACCELERATION together (the scenario-C signature).
Good vs bad: Active = breadth broad+broadening AND trajectory accelerating+sustained.
Drives: The discrete alert: 'debasement thesis at risk — re-weight toward pick-and-shovel'.
Note: Needs BOTH conditions — broad-but-flat or narrow-but-accelerating alone does not break the thesis.

glossary.oil_supply_monitor:
Oil-supply-risk watch — OBJECTIVE proxies (price break · OVX vol · backwardation) that arm the energy-royalty breakdown watch (5.4) when they fire together. It reads the MARKET, never political intent.
Good vs bad: Dormant (glut assumption holds) → ELEVATED (the three proxies fire together → energy-royalty watch armed).
Drives: When elevated, arms the energy-royalty breakdown candidate set (5.4) — never an auto-buy, and tagged outside the core circle.
Note: No component scores intent (the anti-pattern). The headline flag is context only, human-read, never scored.
glossary.oil_price_break:
WTI/Brent through a set threshold — the market re-pricing supply risk into the level.
Good vs bad: Break = WTI ≥ ~85 or Brent ≥ ~90 (tunable). Below = glut intact.
Drives: One of the three objective proxies that must fire together.
glossary.ovx_spike:
OVX — the CBOE crude-oil implied-vol index (the options market pricing a fat oil tail).
Good vs bad: Spike = OVX ≥ ~45 (tunable). Calm = glut / no tail priced.
Drives: The volatility proxy — the options market's read of an oil tail.
glossary.oil_backwardation:
Futures term structure flipping to BACKWARDATION (front richer than deferred) — the cleanest tell of PHYSICAL supply stress / Hormuz fear.
Good vs bad: Backwardation = front − deferred ≥ ~$0.50/bbl. Contango (front cheaper) = glut.
Drives: The physical-stress proxy; with a price break and an OVX spike it arms the watch.
Note: The hardest-to-fake tell — physical buyers paying up for prompt barrels.
glossary.oil_headline:
Ceasefire-violation / Hormuz keyword flag — CONTEXT ONLY, human-read, NEVER scored.
Good vs bad: Present = supply-risk keywords in the feed; tells you WHY oil moved (supply vs demand).
Drives: Renders as context beside the objective trigger; it does NOT move the flag or any score.

glossary.scenario_engine:
The four-scenario robustness lens (A managed-debasement · B fiscal-dominance/bear-steepener · C AI-productivity-WIN · D reflation). Weights are driven by the live signals; names are scored on how they do ACROSS the distribution.
Good vs bad: Per name: robustness = probability-weighted E[payoff] − λ·dispersion. Higher = more all-weather.
Drives: Surfaces the robust ballast vs the convex spear, and the book's scenario gaps — it informs sizing/hedging, it does NOT override the barbell.
Note: Robustness ≠ upside. The spear is MEANT to lose on robustness and win on single-scenario upside — both are reported.
glossary.scenario_weights:
The probability weights on A/B/C/D, driven from a house base prior tilted by the live signals (rates→B, productivity→C, macro→A, copper→D).
Good vs bad: Sum to 1. Rising productivity breadth raises C; a firing bear-steepener raises B.
Drives: The probabilities the per-name robustness is weighted by; the upstream of every P3 number.
glossary.robustness:
A name's probability-weighted expected payoff MINUS a dispersion penalty (λ·weighted stdev across scenarios) — the all-weather score.
Good vs bad: Higher = consistent across futures. A high-upside, high-variance bet scores LOWER than a steady ballast.
Drives: Ranks the book by all-weather fit; pairs with the upside rank, never replaces it.
Note: The dispersion penalty is why the ballast (GROY) tops the spear (AGA.V) here — by design.
glossary.scenario_c_hole:
The scenario-C / uranium hole — the book is structurally under-hedged to the AI-productivity WIN (and reflation); the electrification-royalty slot is the only real C/D hedge.
Good vs bad: Fires when C weight is non-trivial AND the C/D-winning book weight is thin.
Drives: A standing alarm to scout/size the electrification slot — feeds the rotation/replacement work (P5).

scenario_engine.note: robustness ≠ upside — the spear leads on single-scenario upside, the ballast on robustness (by design)

glossary.aga_add_gate:
The proportional-add gate for the convex spear (AGA.V) — three conditions (thesis intact · entry not extended · regime supportive) that must ALL hold to add, sized proportionally and hard-capped at the 60% spear ceiling.
Good vs bad: ADD (all pass, room left) · HOLD (a condition fails) · BLOCKED (at ceiling or invalidated).
Drives: Gates discretionary spear adds; the proposed size scales with condition strength and the posture cap.
Note: An unverifiable condition (no entry read) does NOT green-light an add — silence fails closed.
glossary.invalidation_status:
Per-thesis invalidation / stop lines wired to the SENTINEL flags + per-name forensics.
Good vs bad: INTACT · WATCH (a soft flag touches the thesis) · INVALIDATED (a hard line tripped — exit / rotate).
Drives: Turns a firing flag into a name-level stop action; tailwind flags are context, never stops.
glossary.dry_powder:
Dry-powder deployment — WHERE powder waits (USD/CAD carry tilt) and WHETHER to deploy.
Good vs bad: HOLD (defensive) · DEPLOY (clean entry present) · STAGGER (ladder in). Convexity tranche reserved when crisis (B) weight is rich.
Drives: The standing cash-deployment rule, fed by the carry tilt (P2.3) and the scenario weights (P3).

glossary.thesis_monitor:
The per-name thesis-variable dashboard — the specific variables each holding's thesis lives or dies on, tracked continuously so drift shows before a trip.
Good vs bad: Per name: ON-TRACK (all known healthy) · WATCH (soft drift or a hard unknown) · OFF-TRACK (a hard variable off-track).
Drives: The finer-grained companion to the P4 invalidation lines; a hard variable off-track is the thesis-breaker.
Note: Unknowns never read as healthy — a data gap is a WATCH on a hard variable, not a pass.
